source.title: Lubrication Approximations for Surface Tension Driven Interfaces: Some Open Problems

accepted.question_text: Can one prove finite-time droplet pinch-off in the lubrication approximation for a liquid jet falling from a nozzle, where h is the outer surface radius, x is the axial coordinate, v is the leading-order axial velocity, and the reduced model approximates the three-dimensional Navier-Stokes free-surface equations with gravity, surface tension, density, and viscosity? The target is an analytical proof that the reduced system develops a finite-time singularity corresponding to droplet breakup, rather than only numerical evidence for such a singularity.

evidence.quote: However, no proof of this fact exists.

accepted.question_text: For the same lubrication approximation of an axisymmetric liquid jet before droplet breakup, do solutions remain consistent with the asymptotic approximation by retaining a bounded first spatial derivative of the radius h up to the pinch-off time?

evidence.quote: A conjecture due to CONSTANTIN states that before breakup solutions to (1) retain bounded first derivative in h.

accepted.question_text: In a Hele-Shaw cell treated as a two-dimensional incompressible Darcy free-boundary problem whose boundary pressure is controlled by surface tension, can the evolution produce a finite-time topological singularity in which one connected region of fluid pinches off and becomes two disconnected regions?

evidence.quote: For example, can finite time singularities occur, in which a connected region of fluid separates into two disconnected regions?

accepted.question_text: For the one-dimensional lubrication approximation of a thin neck in a Hele-Shaw cell, with neck thickness h satisfying the reduced local model h_t + (h h_zzz)_z = 0, can one prove the spatial regularity required for the approximation to remain valid as a singularity forms, specifically that h has at least a bounded first spatial derivative up to breakup?

evidence.quote: To respect the approximation, we require the solution to have at least a bounded first derivative as as singularity forms.

accepted.question_text: For fourth-order degenerate thin-film equations for a nonnegative film height h, when the film has compact support and the equation degenerates as h approaches zero at a moving contact line, what boundary conditions should be imposed at the edge of the support so that the contact-line problem is physically and mathematically well posed?

evidence.quote: it is unclear what boundary conditions are required at the edge of the support.

accepted.question_text: For the fourth-order degenerate diffusion model for thin films in which the film height h evolves with a mobility coefficient proportional to a power h^n, is the initial-value problem well posed for nonnegative initial data, despite the absence of an inherent maximum principle for the fourth-order spatial operator?

evidence.quote: there is no inherent maximum principle associated with the spatial operator
the well-posedness of the initial value problem with nonnegative initial data

accepted.question_text: For an unforced one-dimensional fourth-order degenerate lubrication equation for a thin film or Hele-Shaw neck, with film height h and mobility depending on a power of h, can one prove finite-time singularity formation without imposing special forcing boundary conditions?

evidence.quote: a proof of singularity formation for an unforced system

accepted.question_text: For the Cauchy problem on the real line for the fourth-order degenerate thin-film equation with compactly supported nonnegative initial data and mobility depending on a power of h, do weak solutions converge as time grows to the corresponding source-type self-similar solution?

evidence.quote: convergence onto the source type solution for the CAUCHY problem on the line

accepted.question_text: For two-dimensional versions of the fourth-order degenerate lubrication equations for a surface-tension-driven film height h, what analytical theory can be developed for existence, regularity, rupture, and asymptotic behavior, given that the one-dimensional theory does not yet extend to two spatial dimensions?

evidence.quote: In 2D, very little is known about these equations.

needs_review.question_text_raw: Some related problems include models with van der Waals attractions, the interaction of surfactants, and the thin film and Hele-Shaw problems with inertia.

evidence.quote: Some related problems include models with VAN DER WAALS attractions
the thin film and HELE SHAW problems with inertia

trace.notes: Normalized the input as a zbMATH resolver URL for document 1104562.

Direct local network retrieval of zbMATH and API hosts was unavailable in the sandbox. Workspace metadata identified zbMATH 1104562 as Andrea Bertozzi, 'Lubrication approximations for surface tension driven interfaces: Some open problems', with DOI 10.1002/zamm.19960761211.

An exact-title search recovered a readable PDF hosted at the University of Oxford. The PDF's first visible article title matches the zbMATH title and its text contains the open-problem source used for extraction.

Mapped the PDF article structure: title and overview on page 1; Section 1 on droplet breakup on page 1; Section 2 on the Hele-Shaw cell on page 2; Section 3 on thin films, moving contact lines, and fourth-order degenerate diffusion equations on pages 2-3; references begin on page 3.
